subject: Literature
title: The Communist Manifesto
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Communist Manifesto usable.

hook.text: A twenty-three-page pamphlet published in 1848 was banned by nearly every government in Europe within months.

buildup.text: Marx and Engels argued that history was a struggle between classes and that workers would inevitably overthrow capitalism.

discovery.text: The Manifesto was suppressed precisely because its ideas spread fastest among the industrial workers it described.

twist.text: Every ban increased its underground popularity, and by the twentieth century it had reshaped the map of the world.

climax.text: The Communist Manifesto showed that banning political texts can transform obscure pamphlets into world-changing documents.

punchline.text: The most banned pamphlet in history changed the world.

quiz.question: What effect did banning the Communist Manifesto have?
options: It successfully prevented the spread of communist ideas
Each ban increased underground popularity and eventually reshaped the world
It had no noticeable effect on the text's readership
